## Summary Automated nightly sync of `main` into `dev`. - **10 commits** from `main` (`ff20ed546..ed9c2c8c1`), merge-base `f9d9bdcc6` - **`Python lines: +7243 / -1832 across 90 files`** - All files: 104 changed, 7474 insertions(+), 1976 deletions(-) - Merge commit: `a1be423e36be61ad5ff1c9385f6cfc27bd4681d3` (parents: `ff20ed546` dev, `ed9c2c8c1` main) - 33 files conflicted; 35 files have conflict-resolution content in `--remerge-diff` Commits synced from `main`: | SHA | Subject | |---|---| | `ed9c2c8c1` | fix(gtp): preserve scratch lifetime during full-iteration capture (#7780) | | `ea99fdfce` | [DCP V2 3/4] Integrate dynamic CP with standard train and eval schedules (#7047) | | `205276955` | Fix integrity settings during checkpoint conversion (#6502) | | `9ef1a71d6` | Add external code provenance requirements to PR template and agent guidance (#8269) | | `01e36a2a9` | ci: group CPU test selection before the GPU matrix (#8381) | | `0a2f6eec5` | ci(autobot): AUT-2620 allow automation team approvals (#8454) | | `9314b010d` | feat(inference): per-token NVFP4 squared-ReLU and SwiGLU MoE via FlashInfer CuTe DSL (#8262) | | `18bc49d2f` | Gather only the MXFP8 weight planes each compute phase needs in MFSDPv2 (#7907) | | `4422adc5b` | Update copy-pr-bot.yaml [skip ci] | | `7d3f0fb3b` | Inference: remove the disable_ep_consensus flag (#7926) | The dominant change is **Dynamic Context Parallelism V2** (`ea99fdfce`, #7047) — part 3 of a deliberate 4-part upstream redesign. It renames `hybrid_context_parallel` → `dynamic_context_parallel`, restructures `data_schedule.py` / `data_schedule_utils.py`, and moves CP slicing/padding to a single pre-CP-slice step. Most of this PR's conflict surface comes from that one commit. ## Files where main's version was taken wholesale | File | Justification | |---|---| | `.github/copy-pr-bot.yaml` | Trustee roster is owned by main. Main's version removes 5 trustees; each removal has a known main SHA: `aklife97`←`0d698bd27`, `jenchen13`←`fb6a123a0`, `sanandaraj5597`←`06b07a1f5`, `thomasdhc`←`8a9340f6c`, `wplf`←`990ced940`. Also picks up `4422adc5b`. | | `megatron/core/datasets/data_schedule.py` | DCP V2 design (`ea99fdfce`). Per skill guidance, dev's scheduler classes (`BasePackingScheduler`, `DpBalancedScheduler`, `DefaultDynamicCPScheduler`, `wrap_data_iterator`, `get_batch_on_this_rank_for_sequence_packing`) are retained and the legacy main-only scheduling path is **not** appended. | | `megatron/training/datasets/data_samplers.py` | On the skill's override list. Verified post-override: all `args.hybrid_context_parallel` references renamed to `args.dynamic_context_parallel`. | ### Skill override-list entries deliberately NOT applied The skill lists five files to take from main. Three were not taken, with reasons: - **`megatron/training/training.py` — NOT main-wholesale.** Resolved as a true 3-way merge: dev's file as the base, with main's +52/−36 grafted across **7 hunk resolutions**. Taking main wholesale would have dropped 12 dev-only FLOPs/vision symbols and reverted `train_step`'s result tuple from 13 fields to main's narrower shape. The merged file keeps the **13-field `train_step`** contract and grafts main's `wrap_data_iterator(..., pg_collection=get_attr_wrapped_model(model[0], "pg_collection"))` call, since DCP V2 made `pg_collection` a required argument. - **`megatron/training/initialize.py`** — dev is strictly ahead here (dev-only Dynamo cache-limit feature with live callers). Main's version would delete it. Standard merge kept both sides. - **`megatron/core/optimizer/layer_wise_optimizer.py`** — dev's constructor signature is strictly ahead and has live callers in the merged tree. No override. - **`megatron/training/utils.py`** — the override entry is now stale: on dev this path is a **package** (`megatron/training/utils/`), not a module. `git checkout origin/main -- megatron/training/utils.py` is not applicable. ## Files restored | File / symbol | Why | |---|---| | `get_cp_slice_for_thd` (`data_schedule_utils.py`) | Dev-only helper with live references in the merged tree; dropped by conflict resolution. Merge accident → restored. | | `dcp_gpus_needed` (`data_schedule_utils.py`) | Dev-only helper, never on `main`, never on the merge base, zero callers. Main never explicitly removed it → skill default (b), restored. Required adding `ceil`/`log2` to the `math` import. | | `test_scheduler_reroute_rejects_unsupported_sample_keys` (`tests/unit_tests/test_sequence_packing.py`) | Dev-only test dropped in favour of main's multimodal-key variant. A generic unsupported key is a distinct equivalence class — only this test proves the guard rejects on the *key set* rather than on a multimodal allowlist. Restored and verified against the merged assertion text in `data_schedule_utils.py:460`. | ### Files present on main but intentionally not restored - `.github/workflows/multi-approval-bot.yml` — dev removed it deliberately in `2b4b9c428`. - `tests/test_utils/recipes/h100/bert.yaml` — never existed on dev; nothing in the merged tree references it. - `tests/unit_tests/.../test_gated_delta_net2_parallel.py` — dev removed it deliberately in `f4c2ea8ba`. ## Notable conflict resolutions ### DCP V2 (`ea99fdfce`, #7047) — main's design adopted Adopted from main, with this commit as the evidence for each dev-only removal: - `transformer_config.py` / `model_parallel_config.py` validation removals - the `data_schedule.py` / `data_schedule_utils.py` restructure - main's **single pre-CP-slice `pad_packed_batch_before_cp_slice`**, replacing dev's two-stage padding. This drops two dev tests in `test_sequence_packing.py` covering THD tail padding, because the producer-side knobs they exercised (`thd_tail_padding_policy='extend_last'`, `thd_max_packed_sequences`) no longer exist in the new flow. An in-file `NOTE` records this with the SHA. - the CP1 `cp_singleton_group` normalization moving to a new location - the `scheduler_map` enum rekey - int64 coercion of the reroute scalar keys - deletion of `megatron/core/pipeline_parallel/hybrid_cp_schedule.py` (deleted on both sides) - deletion of `broadcast_to_pp_group` (was on the merge base, removed by `ea99fdfce`, zero callers in the merged tree) - the `test_scheduler_reroute_rejects_inconsistent_local_sample_keys` → `test_scheduler_reroute_rejects_inconsistent_sample_keys` rename. Not adopting it also drops main's `test_default_dynamic_cp_scheduler_requires_dynamic_cp`. A `NOTE` in `model_parallel_config.py` documents the divergence; a matching `NOTE` is in `tests/unit_tests/test_model_parallel_config.py`. The `hybrid_cp` → `dynamic_cp` rename keeps back-compat through the existing `@deprecated_hybrid_cp_kwargs` shim (`megatron/core/_batch_api_compat.py`), which aliases `is_hybrid_cp`→`dynamic_cp` and `hybrid_cp_group_func`→`dynamic_cp_group_func` on both `get_batch_on_this_cp_rank` and `get_batches_on_this_cp_rank`. `tests/unit_tests/test_hybrid_context_parallel_args.py` was adapted to expect `DeprecationWarning` rather than dev's `UserWarning`, matching what the shim actually emits. ### `disable_ep_consensus` (`7d3f0fb3b`, #7926) — intentional removal, plus one inconsistency the sync had to finish The advisory audit flagged what looked like a complete dev-only feature being wiped out. It is intentional: main's `7d3f0fb3b` removes the flag and its whole consumer chain. The merge, however, landed it **half-applied** — it took main's deletion in `megatron/training/config/inference_config.py` but kept dev's CLI flag declaration in `megatron/training/arguments.py`, leaving `--inference-disable-ep-consensus` orphaned with no reader anywhere in the tree (`grep` → 0 hits). Deleted the 9-line `add_argument` block to complete main's removal. ### MFSDP V2 (`18bc49d2f`, #7907) `module.py`, `quantized_dbuffer.py`, `parameter_group.py` and 3 test files. Verified in the merged tree: `Phase` has relocated to the new `experimental/phase.py:20` and is imported by `module.py:42` and `parameter_group.py:35`; there are no dangling `QuantizedDBuffer.get_tensor` references after the `get_tensor` → `get_tensor_view` + `update_mxfp8_tensor` migration. The dropped dev test `test_quantized_dbuffer_get_tensor_supports_gemm` was **superseded** by main's rename to `..._updated_tensor_supports_gemm`; restoring dev's version would `AttributeError` against the new API. ### testmon CI (`01e36a2a9`, #8381) `.github/workflows/_unit-tests.yml`, `tests/test_utils/python_scripts/test_testmon_workflow.py`, and `select_unit_tests.py` are all **byte-identical to main** and mutually self-consistent. All 5 CI-config self-tests pass. ### Other - `megatron/elastification/pretrain_hybrid_flex.py` / `pretrain_hybrid.py`: mock-data support now comes from main's `MockGPTDataset` / `MockVarlenDataset` (lines 29, 452-463) rather than dev's `MockSFTDataset`. - `megatron/core/generalized_tensor_parallelism.py`: docstring reflow only. - `skills/nightly-sync/SKILL.md`: resolved to dev's blob, which is strictly ahead — it already contains main's `data_schedule.py` guidance rewrite plus 3 dev-only lines. ### Merge-correctness fixes (not from either side) Three defects the merge itself introduced or would newly expose: 1. **Duplicate `padding_mask_by_layout` keyword** in `megatron/core/models/hybrid/hybrid_block.py` and `shortcut_block.py`. Both sides added the same kwarg in different places; the merge kept both copies. `ast.parse` accepts duplicate call kwargs but `compile()` rejects them, so this would have been an import-time `SyntaxError`. Fixed; an AST-walking audit over all 90 changed files now reports **0 duplicate findings**. 2. **`shortcut_block.py` pylint `E0606`** (`paired_state` possibly-unbound). Pre-existing on *both* dev and main, but CI's pylint only runs on changed `megatron/core` files — this sync changes the file, so it would have newly failed `linting`. Fixed behaviour-preservingly with a `paired_state = None` initialization (the inference path returns early and never reaches the consumer, which is already guarded by `if not inference:`). 3. **`model_parallel_config.py` pylint `C0301`** (101 > 100 chars) in a `NOTE` added by this sync. Reflowed. ## Disposition of pre-push advisory findings The skill's dev-feature-preservation audit reports **1384 candidate dev-only line removals**. Every one is accounted for: - **781** are **formatting/reordering false positives** — the line still exists in the merged tree with different whitespace, wrapping, or ordering. Separated from real drops with an identifier-presence filter (does every identifier on the dev line still appear in the merged file?). - **599** are **identifier-absent** and were categorized into 7 clusters, each resolved with a specific main commit as evidence: 1. `hybrid_cp` → `dynamic_cp` rename — `ea99fdfce`; back-compat retained via the shim. 2. DCP V2 redesign (`data_schedule*.py`, `pretrain_gpt.py`, `pretrain_hybrid.py`, `test_sequence_packing.py`, `parallel_state.py`, `test_schedules.py`) — `ea99fdfce`. 3. MFSDP V2 (`module.py`, `quantized_dbuffer.py`, `parameter_group.py`, 3 test files) — `18bc49d2f`. 4. `disable_ep_consensus` — `7d3f0fb3b`; **one real inconsistency found and fixed** (orphaned CLI flag, above). 5. testmon CI (`_unit-tests.yml`, `test_testmon_workflow.py`, `select_unit_tests.py`) — `01e36a2a9`; all byte-identical to main. 6. GTP `generalized_tensor_parallelism.py` — docstring reflow only. 7. `.github/copy-pr-bot.yaml` trustees — 5 removals, SHAs listed above. - **4** appeared *after* the fix above: they are the `--inference-disable-ep-consensus` block this sync intentionally deleted per `7d3f0fb3b`. Case (a), documented. Guard checks, both clean: - **`.github/CODEOWNERS`** — `git diff origin/dev HEAD -- .github/CODEOWNERS` is **empty** (0 lines). Untouched. - **Dependency triple** (`pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `docker/Dockerfile.ci.dev`) — `git diff origin/dev HEAD` is **empty** (0 lines). Dev's versions kept. - **Git source reconciliation** — `[tool.uv.sources]` is identical on both sides (9 sources each; 0 only-in-main, 0 at differing revisions). No reconciliation needed, so **`uv.lock` was not regenerated**. ## Verification performed **Five static audit layers** over the 90 changed Python files, all clean: | Audit | Result | |---|---| | Import resolution | 6 findings, all false positives — 3 are namespace packages without `__init__.py` (`experimental_attention_variant`, `inference/contexts/attention_context`, `ops`), and `utils.py:572` is inside a `try/except (ImportError, OSError)` that is identical on dev and main | | Attribute-level | 0 real findings | | Symbol-level with live-reference tracing | **0 dropped dev symbols with live references; 0 dropped dev symbols even without references** | | Duplicate param / call-kwarg (AST walk) | **0** (after the `padding_mask_by_layout` fixes) | | Cross-boundary signature / kwarg | 81 findings, all bare-name collisions across unrelated modules (`run`, `log`, `Linear`, `get_world_size`, `scatter`, `gather`, `checkpoint`, `LayerNorm`, `train`, `save`, `write`, `_report`, `get_buffer`). The 2 genuine clusters (`hybrid_cp_group_func`, `is_hybrid_cp` call sites) are covered by the `@deprecated_hybrid_cp_kwargs` shim; main owns all 4 `is_hybrid_cp` call sites and there is no `filterwarnings = error` anywhere in the repo | **pyflakes sweep** over all 90 changed files: no new undefined names. Three pre-existing ones remain, unchanged on both dev and main — `ProcessGroup` ×2 (`megatron/core/utils.py:1521,1522`) and `WandbModule` (`megatron/core/inference/config.py:775`). **The CI `linting` job reproduced locally and green**, with tooling pinned to exactly the repo's versions (`black==26.3.0`, `isort==5.13.2`, `pylint==3.2.6`, `ruff~=0.9.0`): ``` black: 80 files would be left unchanged. isort: OK pylint: no findings ruff: All checks passed! ``` Also verified: all 19 added files carry copyright headers (16 code files checked, 3 non-code skipped). ## Notes - Commits are signed off with `-s` (DCO trailer) only. The bot container has **no GPG key** (`commit.gpgsign` and `user.signingkey` are unset, no secret keys present), so `-S` was not possible. - Formatting was applied in the skill's prescribed order: `black`, then `isort`. ## Phase 3: CI-driven fixes (rolling fix commit) All of the following are in a single rolling fix commit on top of the immutable merge commit. Every item was classified with the skill's provenance test — is this a main *correctness invariant* dev lacked (adopt main, update dev's configs), or main *lacking a feature dev implemented* (restore dev's code on main's structure)? ### Restored: the `prepare_packed_seq_params` frontend hook (merge accident) The most significant find. Dev calls `prepare_packed_seq_params(...)` from the training entrypoints before model forward; the merged tree called it **zero** times: | symbol | dev | main | merged (before fix) | |---|---|---|---| | `prepare_packed_seq_params` call sites in `pretrain_{gpt,hybrid}.py` | 4 | 0 | **0** | | `prebuild_balanced_layouts` | dev-only | 0 | defined, never reached from frontend | | `finalize_packed_seq_params` | dev-only | 0 | defined, called only by the above | Main's DCP V2 rewrite (`ea99fdfce`) replaced both `get_batch` bodies, and since main has no `prepare_packed_seq_params` at all it could not have removed it intentionally — case (b), merge accident. The whole dev-only chain was left dangling in the merged tree while `cp_balanced_indexer.py` still raises *"The frontend must call prebuild_balanced_layouts before model forward."* Restored on **main's** structure, not by reverting it: - `pretrain_gpt.py` — hook re-added after the scheduler call. `data_schedule.py:924` still returns a 7-tuple with `packed_seq_params` at index 5, so dev's `batch[5]` is still correct. - `pretrain_hybrid.py` — main's `return_context_parallel_batch=True` is **main-only API that four of main's own test files depend on**, so the callee keeps ownership of building the `ContextParallelBatch` and the hook runs on the metadata it carries. - `pretrain_hybrid.py::forward_step` — dev carried the hook here too; restored (guarded on `packed_seq_params is not None`) because this covers the non-packing path, whose `ContextParallelBatch` is built locally and never passes through the scheduler branch. ### Restored: varlen-SBHD padding-mask feature, both halves (merge accident) Dev's `use_varlen_dataset and varlen_sbhd_validation` feature was dropped in two places by the same rewrite; the callee in `megatron/core/utils.py` still takes `needs_padding_mask`, so only the caller side was lost. 1. `get_batch` — `needs_padding_mask` plumbing, the `"padding_mask"` batch key, and the middle-PP reduction made defensive (`.get()`); **verified green**, the dev test `test_hybrid_sbhd_validation_broadcasts_padding_mask_on_all_pp_stages` now passes. 2. `is_dataset_built_on_rank` — the merged tree had only `elif is_packed_sequence:`, leaving middle PP stages without a data iterator. This was the root cause of an NCCL `ALLREDUCE` watchdog hang in the `data/**` bucket: the dev test's assertion sits *outside* its `try/finally`, so ranks failing it skipped `destroy_model_parallel()` and desynchronized the *next* test's barrier. Restored → bucket went from hang to `194 passed`. The packing path was never regressed — `padding_mask` occurrences in `data_schedule.py` are identical across dev, main and merged (22/22/22) — so the fix is correctly scoped to the non-packing caller. ### Adopted: main's `calculate_per_token_loss` assert for dynamic CP `TransformerConfig.__post_init__` gained `assert self.calculate_per_token_loss` under `dynamic_context_parallel`. Evidence that this is a genuine main invariant dev already held rather than a regression: dev's own `megatron/training/arguments.py` **already** asserts it at the CLI layer (1 occurrence on dev, 0 on main, 1 merged). So main's config-level assert was adopted and dev's incidental test configs were updated to satisfy it, rather than scoping the assert away. Updated: `test_transformer_config_dynamic_cp.py` (the `dynamic-cp1` fixture param, covering every test using it), `test_csa_builder_contract_cpu.py`, `test_transformer_layer.py`, `test_attention_variant_dsa.py`, `test_cp_balanced_indexer_layout.py`. The exposure was closed by sweeping all of `tests/` plus the functional recipes rather than one CI bucket per cycle. Sites verified *safe* and deliberately left alone: `SimpleNamespace` / args mocks, `ModelParallelConfig` (same field, no such assert), `initialize_model_parallel` kwargs, static-method validators such as `_validate_dsv4_execution_scope`, `pytest.raises`-wrapped constructions where dev's `ValueError` fires before main's assert, and functional configs that already pass `--calculate-per-token-loss`. The CUDA-graph half of the same guard was **scoped** rather than adopted, since dev implements packed-DSA-CP CUDA graphs that main lacks; main's rejection tests still pass. ### Fixed: stale mock targets in dev tests against main's renamed symbols - `test_get_batch.py` — main imports the MTP helper under an alias (`mtp_on_this_rank as mtp_on_this_rank_func`) and `pretrain_gpt.get_batch` binds a local of the un-aliased name, so the dev test's `monkeypatch.setattr(pretrain_gpt, "mtp_on_this_rank", ...)` would raise `AttributeError`. Retargeted to the alias. This test had not yet run on any CI cycle (testmon selection), so it was a latent failure. - `test_get_batch.py` — the hybrid scheduler stub now returns a `ContextParallelBatch`, which is what the real callee returns under main's `return_context_parallel_batch=True`. All behavioural assertions are unchanged; the test still pins the hook to the normalized `TransformerConfig` rather than raw args. ### Dev-feature audit delta The advisory audit total fell **1379 → 1353** over Phase 3 as these restorations landed (`pretrain_hybrid.py` alone: 70 → 66). The remaining lines were reviewed and are main's DCP V2 structural rewrite or cosmetic differences. Specifically re-checked and confirmed benign: `logits_load_dir` (2/2/2), `logits_saver` (2/2/2), `_build_cached_logits_loss_func` (present, main's expanded docstring), and `stimer` (dev's `global` declaration was read-only, so main's removal is behaviour-neutral). `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `docker/Dockerfile.ci.dev` were re-verified byte-identical to dev before every push. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ### Phase 3 — cycle on `77a7c3a27` (prev `3b8b442d1`) Two failures on `3b8b442d1`, both **sync-caused and fixed**. The full 117-context matrix was allowed to drain before pushing so both were caught in one cycle rather than two. **1. `test_get_batch.py::test_hybrid_thd_forward_prebuilds_batch_metadata_once`** `KeyError: 'pg_collection'`. Main's DCP V2 (`ea99fdfce`) made `forward_step` pass the model's collection down to `get_batch`, so it now requests a third attribute through `get_attr_wrapped_model`: | `get_attr_wrapped_model(model, ...)` in `pretrain_hybrid.forward_step` | dev | main | merged | |---|---|---|---| | `vp_stage` | yes | yes | yes | | `config` | yes | yes | yes | | `pg_collection` | **no** | **yes** | **yes** | Genuine main addition, correctly adopted. The dev-only test's stub was a two-key dict literal, so the third lookup raised `KeyError`. Added `"pg_collection": None` — the value the real explicit-group path treats as "bootstrap from MPU globals", and `get_batch` is mocked in that test, so it is never dereferenced. No assertion changed. Swept `tests/` for the same shape: this is the only `get_attr_wrapped_model` stub built as a dict literal that can `KeyError`; every other stub is permissive (`getattr`, `Mock()`, `SimpleNamespace`). The only other caller of `forward_step`, `test_packed_pretrain_process_groups.py:117`, already supplies `pg_collection=pgs` and passed. **2. `test_transformer_config_dynamic_cp.py::test_head_divisibility_uses_configured_cp[1-1-True-1-False]`** `AssertionError: Dynamic context parallelism must be used with calculate_per_token_loss`. | | dev | main | merged | |---|---|---|---| | the `calculate_per_token_loss` guard in `transformer_config.py` | 0 | **1** | 1 | | main's pinning test `test_dynamic_cp_rejects_unsupported_config` | 0 | **1** | 1 | | the failing file `test_transformer_config_dynamic_cp.py` | **1** | absent | 1 | A **genuine new main correctness invariant** — a loss normalized by a static token count is wrong once the CP group size varies per microbatch — not main lacking a dev feature. Resolution is therefore *adopt main's guard, update dev's test configs*: `_make_config` now applies `kwargs.setdefault("calculate_per_token_loss", True)` when dynamic CP is requested. Set as a default, not forced, so an explicit override still wins and main's guard stays testable. The file's fixture path already carried this flag from an earlier cycle for this same guard, so the helper fix makes the direct `_make_config` callers consistent with it. Audited every other test that builds a config with `dynamic_context_parallel=True` (16 files). Two could in principle reach the guard; both are safe and unchanged: - `test_model_parallel_config.py` — its dynamic-CP sites construct `ModelParallelConfig`, which does not run `TransformerConfig.__post_init__`. - `test_dsv4_hybrid_attention.py:171` — dev's DSv4 guard at `transformer_config.py:2773` fires before main's at 4703, so its `pytest.raises(ValueError, ...)` still matches. Bucket concluded `success`. Note on selection: only 2 of the 9 `test_head_divisibility_uses_configured_cp` parametrizations were selected this run (testmon deselected 15 in that bucket), which is why a guard affecting every `dynamic_cp=True` case surfaced as a single failure. Fixing it in the helper covers the unselected ones too. **Advisory audit:** CODEOWNERS and the dependency triple (`pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `docker/Dockerfile.ci.dev`) all byte-identical to dev. Dev-feature audit 1355 → **1356**; the +1 is exactly the two-key `return {"vp_stage": None, "config": config}[attr]` stub line replaced in fix 1 above. The count rises rather than falls because these fixes adopt main's structure with new `NOTE(nightly-sync 26_10_2026)` comments instead of re-adding dev's literal lines — each remaining finding in the touched files is an intentional, commented adaptation, not a dropped dev feature. ### Phase 3 — cycle on `6202f9599` (prev `77a7c3a27`) Both previous failures fixed (data bucket 200 → 205 passed, transformer bucket green). One newly-selected test exposed a **merge misalignment in `test_get_batch.py`**, fixed in all four affected places. `test_sft_batch[1024-1-1-1]`: `assert padding_mask is None` failed on `tensor([[0, 129, 242, 498, 1024]])` — i.e. `padding_mask` was bound to `cu_seqlens`' value. Cause: four tests unpack the batch positionally against `pretrain_hybrid.BATCH_KEYS`: ```python (attention_mask, padding_mask, cu_seqlens, ...) = [batch[key] for key in pretrain_hybrid.BATCH_KEYS] ``` `BATCH_KEYS` is a **main-only** convention (`ea99fdfce`; it does not exist on dev in either entrypoint) and is sorted, so the restored dev-only `padding_mask` key belongs between `max_seqlen` and `position_ids`. Main's own version of these tests unpacks ten names with no `padding_mask`; the merge spliced dev's name in **second**, which silently shifted eight of the eleven bindings by one: | index | name bound | actual key | | |---|---|---|---| | 0 | `attention_mask` | `attention_mask` | ok | | 1 | `padding_mask` | `cu_seqlens` | wrong | | 2–8 | `cu_seqlens` … `max_seqlen` | each shifted by one | wrong | | 9, 10 | `position_ids`, `tokens` | correct | ok | Only `test_sft_batch` was selected this run; the other three (`test_get_batch.py:1028`, `:1645`, `:2056`) were latently broken the same way and are fixed too. Reordered the names to follow `BATCH_KEYS` rather than renumbering the key, since sorted order is main's own convention and the production consumers already follow it. Verified afterwards that all four unpacks now read `attention_mask, cu_seqlens, cu_seqlens_padded, hybrid_cp_group, labels, local_cp_size, loss_mask, max_seqlen, padding_mask, position_ids, tokens`, and that `pretrain_gpt.forward_step`'s own `BATCH_KEYS` branch already matched (its 6-/7-tuple branches use separate dev-only batch shapes and do not collide at 11). **Advisory audit:** CODEOWNERS and the dependency triple byte-identical to dev; dev-feature audit unchanged at 1356.

## Phase 3 — CI fix commit `b24bdac31`

All nine non-exempt failures from the first CI cycle are addressed by one rolling fix
commit on top of the immutable merge commit `a1be423e3` (2-commit policy preserved).

### Merge accidents — dev-only hardening restored

Main never removed these lines; the merge dropped them because main happened to own
nearby lines. Restored verbatim from `origin/dev`.

| File | What was dropped | Detected by |
|---|---|---|
| `pretrain_gpt.py`, `pretrain_hybrid.py` | Dev's narrowed ModelOpt import guard. The merge took main's bare `except ImportError:`, which silently disables ModelOpt when an **internal** `megatron.post_training` import fails. Dev inspects `error.name` and re-raises anything that is not `modelopt`/`modelopt.*`. | `post_training/test_modelopt_import_guard.py::test_modelopt_import_guards_only_suppress_missing_modelopt` (`assert None == 'error'`) |

`megatron/elastification/pretrain_hybrid_flex.py` was checked for the same pattern: it
carries the bare `except ImportError:` on **both** dev and main, so it is not an accident
and was left alone.

### Duplicate test-recipe entry

`tests/test_utils/recipes/gb200/unit-tests.yaml` contained the
`ssm/test_gated_delta_net.py` product block twice. The GB200 dispatcher therefore emitted
two jobs for one bucket — the second resolving to `0 workloads` — and the duplication also
violated the one-bucket-per-file scope contract. Removing the duplicate fixes three
failures at once:

- `Unit tests (GB200) / tests/unit_tests/ssm/test_gated_delta_net.py` (both instances)
- `Unit tests (H100) / tests/unit_tests/**/*.py` →
  `test_unit_test_scope_contracts.py::test_every_unit_file_has_exactly_one_platform_bucket[gb200]`

An audit across every recipe YAML found this as the only duplicate.

### Cross-side API reconciliation

**`megatron/core/transformer/transformer_config.py` — DSv4 + dynamic CP.**
Main added an unconditional `raise ValueError("DSv4 dynamic context parallelism is not
supported yet.")`. Dev has since implemented that combination for the balanced zigzag
indexer: dev's own `dsa_cp_balance_indexer` precondition, a few hundred lines above in the
same merged file, explicitly accepts `dynamic_context_parallel=True` as a valid CP
activation. The merged tree ended up carrying two contradictory tests:

- `test_dsv4_hybrid_attention.py::test_config_rejects_dynamic_context_parallel` (main-only) — expects the raise
- `test_cp_balanced_indexer_layout.py::test_balanced_config_accepts_dynamic_context_parallelism` (dev-only) — expects acceptance

The guard is now scoped with `and not self.dsa_cp_balance_indexer`. Since
`dsa_cp_balance_indexer` defaults to `False` and main's test does not set it, main's
rejection still fires for the configurations it was written for, while dev's balanced path
is preserved. Both tests pass. Dev's test file was authored by the dev commits
`6e8ff3ecd` ("Preserve dev DSv4 execution and Muon split-QKV semantics") and `bd23668a4`
("fix: reconcile sync runtime and unit-test integration") — i.e. dev's position here was
established deliberately to survive main syncs.

**`megatron/core/utils.py` — `cp_group is None` fallback.**
Dev's `get_batch_on_this_cp_rank` resolves a missing `cp_group` from `parallel_state`;
main has no fallback and lets `None` reach `torch.distributed.get_world_size(None)` (the
default group). Keeping dev's fallback made main's new
`data/test_batch_api_compat.py` assert, because it calls the helper with no `cp_group` and
no CP initialization. The fallback now probes with `check_initialized=False`, which keeps
it useful once CP is initialized and matches main's behaviour when it is not. All 8
production callers pass `cp_group` explicitly, so this path is only reached by the
compat API.

### Test stubs/configs updated for main's new invariants

- `tests/unit_tests/models/test_hybrid_hash_routing.py`: main added
  `ContextParallelLayoutState.get_layer_padding_mask` plus three call sites
  (`hybrid_block.py`, `shortcut_block.py`, `recompute.py`). Dev's `SimpleNamespace` fake of
  that state predates the method, so `hybrid_block.py:812` raised `AttributeError`. The
  stub now mirrors the real contract (fall back to the single mask when there are no
  per-layout masks).
- `tests/unit_tests/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/test_attention_variant_dsa.py`:
  set `calculate_per_token_loss=True`. Main's new assert requires it under dynamic CP
  because loss scaling cannot use the static TP×CP group when the CP group is chosen per
  microbatch. It does not affect the QKV/RoPE paths under test, and is set on both the
  config and the reference config so they differ only in CP size. This is a genuine
  correctness invariant from main, so it was adopted rather than scoped.

### Pre-push advisory findings

`.github/CODEOWNERS`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, and `docker/Dockerfile.ci.dev` are all
byte-identical to `origin/dev`. The dev-feature audit reports **1377** potential dev-only
line removals, down from 1384 at the Phase 1 push:

- **−8** the ModelOpt guard lines restored above (4 lines × 2 entrypoints)
- **+1** the `utils.py` line reworked above (`get_context_parallel_group()` →
  `get_context_parallel_group(check_initialized=False)`)

The remaining 1377 are the same set dispositioned in the PR description: 781 are
reformatting/reordering artifacts of the `comm`-based line comparison, 599 fall into 7
clusters where the line still exists in the merged tree in a renamed or reflowed form, and
4 are the intentional `--inference-disable-ep-consensus` removals evidenced by main commit
`7d3f0fb3b` (#7926).

### Known structurally-red checks

`DCO` and `DCO gate` are red and cannot be fixed from a sync PR: the failures come from
**upstream main commits** whose `Signed-off-by` name does not exactly match the commit
author. A sync PR necessarily contains main's commits, so it inherits their verdict.
Verified against recently merged sync PRs: **#8402** and **#8209** both merged with
`DCO = ACTION_REQUIRED`, and **#8461** merged with `DCO gate = FAILURE` while `DCO` itself
was `SUCCESS`. Making these green would require rewriting other authors' commit metadata
or filing DCO remediation attestations on their behalf, which this bot will not do.

The retained graph inputs still require fixed `cu_seqlens` capacity and `max_seqlen`. An isolated execution of the padding function with tensor stubs produced 4/5 metadata entries for two packs with a configured capacity of 9, with differing maximum lengths. Please adapt the fixed-metadata handling to the single pre-CP padding stage and preserve the tail-policy tests.

2. **Contiguous layout tagging:** `context_parallel/utils.py::_build_packed_seq_params` lost dev's `cp_partition_mode=layout`. The retained dataclass defaults to `zigzag`, so contiguous Hybrid THD batches fail the DSv4/CSA layout guard at CP>1. Please restore the correct physical-layout metadata; the GPT scheduler's contiguous slicing path also needs checking, rather than changing labels alone.

3. **DSA route preparation:** both pretrain entrypoints lost their `prepare_packed_seq_params()` calls without a replacement production call. The graph-dynamic DSA consumer still requires the per-pack route from `prebuild_balanced_layouts()` and raises when it is absent. Please restore preparation for the applicable layout metadata before forward/capture, adapting it to the new batch API.

4. **SBHD validation masks:** the new entrypoint/TP-helper path drops dev's `needs_padding_mask` transport and excludes middle PP stages from the varlen SBHD dataset path. The dataset and MoE mask consumers remain. Please preserve the mask schema, TP broadcast and intermediate-stage access for `--use-varlen-dataset --varlen-sbhd-validation`; masking only the final loss does not replace that contract.

5. **Static `default_dynamic_cp`:** configuration deliberately keeps this mode legal with `dynamic_context_parallel=False`, but `wrap_data_iterator()` now unconditionally requires `pg_collection.dynamic_cp`, which initialization leaves empty in that mode. An isolated wrapper probe reaches the scheduler on dev but raises before it on this head, even at DP1/CP1. Please preserve a working static path or make an explicit, consistently validated compatibility decision.

6. **Repeated replay:** please retain `dict(next(data_iterator))` in the packed-batch consumer. `RerunDataIterator` copies only when first saving a batch; replay returns the saved dictionary itself. The consumer then rebinds entries to reshaped/sliced tensors, corrupting the next replay. An isolated iterator/consumer probe passes repeated reads on dev but hits the 1-D tokens assertion on the second replay here. This needs consumer-side copy protection and repeated-rewind coverage.

7. **NVFP4 dependency:** the incoming FlashInfer path requires `>=0.7.0`, while the retained dev constraint is `<0.7.0` and the lock pins `0.6.18.post1`. The new feature therefore cannot run in the declared dependency environment. Please reconcile this requirement within the dev dependency setup, preserving unrelated dev dependencies; matching git-source entries alone does not establish compatibility.

It renames `hybrid_context_parallel` → `dynamic_context_parallel`, restructures `data_schedule.py` / `data_schedule_utils.py`, and moves CP slicing/padding to a single pre-CP-slice step. Most of this PR's conflict surface comes from that one commit. ## Files where main's version was taken wholesale | File | Justification | |---|---| | `.github/copy-pr-bot.yaml` | Trustee roster is owned by main. Main's version removes 5 trustees; each removal has a known main SHA: `aklife97`←`0d698bd27`, `jenchen13`←`fb6a123a0`, `sanandaraj5597`←`06b07a1f5`, `thomasdhc`←`8a9340f6c`, `wplf`←`990ced940`. Three were not taken, with reasons: - **`megatron/training/training.py` — NOT main-wholesale.** Resolved as a true 3-way merge: dev's file as the base, with main's +52/−36 grafted across **7 hunk resolutions**. Taking main wholesale would have dropped 12 dev-only FLOPs/vision symbols and reverted `train_step`'s result tuple from 13 fields to main's narrower shape. Merge accident → restored. | | `dcp_gpus_needed` (`data_schedule_utils.py`) | Dev-only helper, never on `main`, never on the merge base, zero callers. Main never explicitly removed it → skill default (b), restored. Required adding `ceil`/`log2` to the `math` import. | | `test_scheduler_reroute_rejects_unsupported_sample_keys` (`tests/unit_tests/test_sequence_packing.py`) | Dev-only test dropped in favour of main's multimodal-key variant. A generic unsupported key is a distinct equivalence class — only this test proves the guard rejects on the *key set* rather than on a multimodal allowlist. Restored and verified against the merged assertion text in `data_schedule_utils.py:460`. | ### Files present on main but intentionally not restored - `.github/workflows/multi-approval-bot.yml` — dev removed it deliberately in `2b4b9c428`. - `tests/test_utils/recipes/h100/bert.yaml` — never existed on dev; nothing in the merged tree references it. - `tests/unit_tests/.../test_gated_delta_net2_parallel.py` — dev removed it deliberately in `f4c2ea8ba`. ## Notable conflict resolutions ### DCP V2 (`ea99fdfce`, #7047) — main's design adopted Adopted from main, with this commit as the evidence for each dev-only removal: - `transformer_config.py` / `model_parallel_config.py` validation removals - the `data_schedule.py` / `data_schedule_utils.py` restructure - main's **single pre-CP-slice `pad_packed_batch_before_cp_slice`**, replacing dev's two-stage padding. A `NOTE` in `model_parallel_config.py` documents the divergence; a matching `NOTE` is in `tests/unit_tests/test_model_parallel_config.py`. The `hybrid_cp` → `dynamic_cp` rename keeps back-compat through the existing `@deprecated_hybrid_cp_kwargs` shim (`megatron/core/_batch_api_compat.py`), which aliases `is_hybrid_cp`→`dynamic_cp` and `hybrid_cp_group_func`→`dynamic_cp_group_func` on both `get_batch_on_this_cp_rank` and `get_batches_on_this_cp_rank`. `tests/unit_tests/test_hybrid_context_parallel_args.py` was adapted to expect `DeprecationWarning` rather than dev's `UserWarning`, matching what the shim actually emits. ### `disable_ep_consensus` (`7d3f0fb3b`, #7926) — intentional removal, plus one inconsistency the sync had to finish The advisory audit flagged what looked like a complete dev-only feature being wiped out. It is intentional: main's `7d3f0fb3b` removes the flag and its whole consumer chain. The merge, however, landed it **half-applied** — it took main's deletion in `megatron/training/config/inference_config.py` but kept dev's CLI flag declaration in `megatron/training/arguments.py`, leaving `--inference-disable-ep-consensus` orphaned with no reader anywhere in the tree (`grep` → 0 hits). Deleted the 9-line `add_argument` block to complete main's removal. ### MFSDP V2 (`18bc49d2f`, #7907) `module.py`, `quantized_dbuffer.py`, `parameter_group.py` and 3 test files. Verified in the merged tree: `Phase` has relocated to the new `experimental/phase.py:20` and is imported by `module.py:42` and `parameter_group.py:35`; there are no dangling `QuantizedDBuffer.get_tensor` references after the `get_tensor` → `get_tensor_view` + `update_mxfp8_tensor` migration. All 5 CI-config self-tests pass. ### Other - `megatron/elastification/pretrain_hybrid_flex.py` / `pretrain_hybrid.py`: mock-data support now comes from main's `MockGPTDataset` / `MockVarlenDataset` (lines 29, 452-463) rather than dev's `MockSFTDataset`. - `megatron/core/generalized_tensor_parallelism.py`: docstring reflow only. - `skills/nightly-sync/SKILL.md`: resolved to dev's blob, which is strictly ahead — it already contains main's `data_schedule.py` guidance rewrite plus 3 dev-only lines. ### Merge-correctness fixes (not from either side) Three defects the merge itself introduced or would newly expose: 1. **Duplicate `padding_mask_by_layout` keyword** in `megatron/core/models/hybrid/hybrid_block.py` and `shortcut_block.py`. Both sides added the same kwarg in different places; the merge kept both copies. `ast.parse` accepts duplicate call kwargs but `compile()` rejects them, so this would have been an import-time `SyntaxError`. Fixed; an AST-walking audit over all 90 changed files now reports **0 duplicate findings**. 2. **`shortcut_block.py` pylint `E0606`** (`paired_state` possibly-unbound). Pre-existing on *both* dev and main, but CI's pylint only runs on changed `megatron/core` files — this sync changes the file, so it would have newly failed `linting`. Fixed behaviour-preservingly with a `paired_state = None` initialization (the inference path returns early and never reaches the consumer, which is already guarded by `if not inference:`). 3. **`model_parallel_config.py` pylint `C0301`** (101 > 100 chars) in a `NOTE` added by this sync. Reflowed. ## Disposition of pre-push advisory findings The skill's dev-feature-preservation audit reports **1384 candidate dev-only line removals**. Every one is accounted for: - **781** are **formatting/reordering false positives** — the line still exists in the merged tree with different whitespace, wrapping, or ordering. Separated from real drops with an identifier-presence filter (does every identifier on the dev line still appear in the merged file?). - **599** are **identifier-absent** and were categorized into 7 clusters, each resolved with a specific main commit as evidence: 1. `hybrid_cp` → `dynamic_cp` rename — `ea99fdfce`; back-compat retained via the shim. 2. DCP V2 redesign (`data_schedule*.py`, `pretrain_gpt.py`, `pretrain_hybrid.py`, `test_sequence_packing.py`, `parallel_state.py`, `test_schedules.py`) — `ea99fdfce`. 3. MFSDP V2 (`module.py`, `quantized_dbuffer.py`, `parameter_group.py`, 3 test files) — `18bc49d2f`. 4. `disable_ep_consensus` — `7d3f0fb3b`; **one real inconsistency found and fixed** (orphaned CLI flag, above). 5. testmon CI (`_unit-tests.yml`, `test_testmon_workflow.py`, `select_unit_tests.py`) — `01e36a2a9`; all byte-identical to main. 6. GTP `generalized_tensor_parallelism.py` — docstring reflow only. 7. `.github/copy-pr-bot.yaml` trustees — 5 removals, SHAs listed above. - **4** appeared *after* the fix above: they are the `--inference-disable-ep-consensus` block this sync intentionally deleted per `7d3f0fb3b`. The bot container has **no GPG key** (`commit.gpgsign` and `user.signingkey` are unset, no secret keys present), so `-S` was not possible. - Formatting was applied in the skill's prescribed order: `black`, then `isort`. ## Phase 3: CI-driven fixes (rolling fix commit) All of the following are in a single rolling fix commit on top of the immutable merge commit. Every item was classified with the skill's provenance test — is this a main *correctness invariant* dev lacked (adopt main, update dev's configs), or main *lacking a feature dev implemented* (restore dev's code on main's structure)? ### Restored: the `prepare_packed_seq_params` frontend hook (merge accident) The most significant find. Dev calls `prepare_packed_seq_params(...)` from the training entrypoints before model forward; the merged tree called it **zero** times: | symbol | dev | main | merged (before fix) | |---|---|---|---| | `prepare_packed_seq_params` call sites in `pretrain_{gpt,hybrid}.py` | 4 | 0 | **0** | | `prebuild_balanced_layouts` | dev-only | 0 | defined, never reached from frontend | | `finalize_packed_seq_params` | dev-only | 0 | defined, called only by the above | Main's DCP V2 rewrite (`ea99fdfce`) replaced both `get_batch` bodies, and since main has no `prepare_packed_seq_params` at all it could not have removed it intentionally — case (b), merge accident. The whole dev-only chain was left dangling in the merged tree while `cp_balanced_indexer.py` still raises *"The frontend must call prebuild_balanced_layouts before model forward."* Restored on **main's** structure, not by reverting it: - `pretrain_gpt.py` — hook re-added after the scheduler call. `data_schedule.py:924` still returns a 7-tuple with `packed_seq_params` at index 5, so dev's `batch[5]` is still correct. - `pretrain_hybrid.py` — main's `return_context_parallel_batch=True` is **main-only API that four of main's own test files depend on**, so the callee keeps ownership of building the `ContextParallelBatch` and the hook runs on the metadata it carries. - `pretrain_hybrid.py::forward_step` — dev carried the hook here too; restored (guarded on `packed_seq_params is not None`) because this covers the non-packing path, whose `ContextParallelBatch` is built locally and never passes through the scheduler branch. ### Restored: varlen-SBHD padding-mask feature, both halves (merge accident) Dev's `use_varlen_dataset and varlen_sbhd_validation` feature was dropped in two places by the same rewrite; the callee in `megatron/core/utils.py` still takes `needs_padding_mask`, so only the caller side was lost. 1. `get_batch` — `needs_padding_mask` plumbing, the `"padding_mask"` batch key, and the middle-PP reduction made defensive (`.get()`); **verified green**, the dev test `test_hybrid_sbhd_validation_broadcasts_padding_mask_on_all_pp_stages` now passes. 2. `is_dataset_built_on_rank` — the merged tree had only `elif is_packed_sequence:`, leaving middle PP stages without a data iterator. Restored → bucket went from hang to `194 passed`. The packing path was never regressed — `padding_mask` occurrences in `data_schedule.py` are identical across dev, main and merged (22/22/22) — so the fix is correctly scoped to the non-packing caller. ### Adopted: main's `calculate_per_token_loss` assert for dynamic CP `TransformerConfig.__post_init__` gained `assert self.calculate_per_token_loss` under `dynamic_context_parallel`. Evidence that this is a genuine main invariant dev already held rather than a regression: dev's own `megatron/training/arguments.py` **already** asserts it at the CLI layer (1 occurrence on dev, 0 on main, 1 merged). So main's config-level assert was adopted and dev's incidental test configs were updated to satisfy it, rather than scoping the assert away. Updated: `test_transformer_config_dynamic_cp.py` (the `dynamic-cp1` fixture param, covering every test using it), `test_csa_builder_contract_cpu.py`, `test_transformer_layer.py`, `test_attention_variant_dsa.py`, `test_cp_balanced_indexer_layout.py`. The exposure was closed by sweeping all of `tests/` plus the functional recipes rather than one CI bucket per cycle. Sites verified *safe* and deliberately left alone: `SimpleNamespace` / args mocks, `ModelParallelConfig` (same field, no such assert), `initialize_model_parallel` kwargs, static-method validators such as `_validate_dsv4_execution_scope`, `pytest.raises`-wrapped constructions where dev's `ValueError` fires before main's assert, and functional configs that already pass `--calculate-per-token-loss`. The CUDA-graph half of the same guard was **scoped** rather than adopted, since dev implements packed-DSA-CP CUDA graphs that main lacks; main's rejection tests still pass. ### Fixed: stale mock targets in dev tests against main's renamed symbols - `test_get_batch.py` — main imports the MTP helper under an alias (`mtp_on_this_rank as mtp_on_this_rank_func`) and `pretrain_gpt.get_batch` binds a local of the un-aliased name, so the dev test's `monkeypatch.setattr(pretrain_gpt, "mtp_on_this_rank", ...)` would raise `AttributeError`. Retargeted to the alias. This test had not yet run on any CI cycle (testmon selection), so it was a latent failure. - `test_get_batch.py` — the hybrid scheduler stub now returns a `ContextParallelBatch`, which is what the real callee returns under main's `return_context_parallel_batch=True`. All behavioural assertions are unchanged; the test still pins the hook to the normalized `TransformerConfig` rather than raw args. ### Dev-feature audit delta The advisory audit total fell **1379 → 1353** over Phase 3 as these restorations landed (`pretrain_hybrid.py` alone: 70 → 66). The remaining lines were reviewed and are main's DCP V2 structural rewrite or cosmetic differences. Specifically re-checked and confirmed benign: `logits_load_dir` (2/2/2), `logits_saver` (2/2/2), `_build_cached_logits_loss_func` (present, main's expanded docstring), and `stimer` (dev's `global` declaration was read-only, so main's removal is behaviour-neutral). `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `docker/Dockerfile.ci.dev` were re-verified byte-identical to dev before every push. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ### Phase 3 — cycle on `77a7c3a27` (prev `3b8b442d1`) Two failures on `3b8b442d1`, both **sync-caused and fixed**. The full 117-context matrix was allowed to drain before pushing so both were caught in one cycle rather than two. **1. `test_get_batch.py::test_hybrid_thd_forward_prebuilds_batch_metadata_once`** `KeyError: 'pg_collection'`. Main's DCP V2 (`ea99fdfce`) made `forward_step` pass the model's collection down to `get_batch`, so it now requests a third attribute through `get_attr_wrapped_model`: | `get_attr_wrapped_model(model, ...)` in `pretrain_hybrid.forward_step` | dev | main | merged | |---|---|---|---| | `vp_stage` | yes | yes | yes | | `config` | yes | yes | yes | | `pg_collection` | **no** | **yes** | **yes** | Genuine main addition, correctly adopted. The dev-only test's stub was a two-key dict literal, so the third lookup raised `KeyError`. Added `"pg_collection": None` — the value the real explicit-group path treats as "bootstrap from MPU globals", and `get_batch` is mocked in that test, so it is never dereferenced. No assertion changed. Swept `tests/` for the same shape: this is the only `get_attr_wrapped_model` stub built as a dict literal that can `KeyError`; every other stub is permissive (`getattr`, `Mock()`, `SimpleNamespace`). The only other caller of `forward_step`, `test_packed_pretrain_process_groups.py:117`, already supplies `pg_collection=pgs` and passed. **2. `test_transformer_config_dynamic_cp.py::test_head_divisibility_uses_configured_cp[1-1-True-1-False]`** `AssertionError: Dynamic context parallelism must be used with calculate_per_token_loss`. | | dev | main | merged | |---|---|---|---| | the `calculate_per_token_loss` guard in `transformer_config.py` | 0 | **1** | 1 | | main's pinning test `test_dynamic_cp_rejects_unsupported_config` | 0 | **1** | 1 | | the failing file `test_transformer_config_dynamic_cp.py` | **1** | absent | 1 | A **genuine new main correctness invariant** — a loss normalized by a static token count is wrong once the CP group size varies per microbatch — not main lacking a dev feature. Resolution is therefore *adopt main's guard, update dev's test configs*: `_make_config` now applies `kwargs.setdefault("calculate_per_token_loss", True)` when dynamic CP is requested. Set as a default, not forced, so an explicit override still wins and main's guard stays testable. The file's fixture path already carried this flag from an earlier cycle for this same guard, so the helper fix makes the direct `_make_config` callers consistent with it. Audited every other test that builds a config with `dynamic_context_parallel=True` (16 files). Two could in principle reach the guard; both are safe and unchanged: - `test_model_parallel_config.py` — its dynamic-CP sites construct `ModelParallelConfig`, which does not run `TransformerConfig.__post_init__`. - `test_dsv4_hybrid_attention.py:171` — dev's DSv4 guard at `transformer_config.py:2773` fires before main's at 4703, so its `pytest.raises(ValueError, ...)` still matches. Bucket concluded `success`. Note on selection: only 2 of the 9 `test_head_divisibility_uses_configured_cp` parametrizations were selected this run (testmon deselected 15 in that bucket), which is why a guard affecting every `dynamic_cp=True` case surfaced as a single failure. Fixing it in the helper covers the unselected ones too. **Advisory audit:** CODEOWNERS and the dependency triple (`pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `docker/Dockerfile.ci.dev`) all byte-identical to dev. Dev-feature audit 1355 → **1356**; the +1 is exactly the two-key `return {"vp_stage": None, "config": config}[attr]` stub line replaced in fix 1 above. The count rises rather than falls because these fixes adopt main's structure with new `NOTE(nightly-sync 26_10_2026)` comments instead of re-adding dev's literal lines — each remaining finding in the touched files is an intentional, commented adaptation, not a dropped dev feature. ### Phase 3 — cycle on `6202f9599` (prev `77a7c3a27`) Both previous failures fixed (data bucket 200 → 205 passed, transformer bucket green). One newly-selected test exposed a **merge misalignment in `test_get_batch.py`**, fixed in all four affected places. `test_sft_batch[1024-1-1-1]`: `assert padding_mask is None` failed on `tensor([[0, 129, 242, 498, 1024]])` — i.e. `padding_mask` was bound to `cu_seqlens`' value. Cause: four tests unpack the batch positionally against `pretrain_hybrid.BATCH_KEYS`: ```python (attention_mask, padding_mask, cu_seqlens, ...) = [batch[key] for key in pretrain_hybrid.BATCH_KEYS] ``` `BATCH_KEYS` is a **main-only** convention (`ea99fdfce`; it does not exist on dev in either entrypoint) and is sorted, so the restored dev-only `padding_mask` key belongs between `max_seqlen` and `position_ids`. Main's own version of these tests unpacks ten names with no `padding_mask`; the merge spliced dev's name in **second**, which silently shifted eight of the eleven bindings by one: | index | name bound | actual key | | |---|---|---|---| | 0 | `attention_mask` | `attention_mask` | ok | | 1 | `padding_mask` | `cu_seqlens` | wrong | | 2–8 | `cu_seqlens` … `max_seqlen` | each shifted by one | wrong | | 9, 10 | `position_ids`, `tokens` | correct | ok | Only `test_sft_batch` was selected this run; the other three (`test_get_batch.py:1028`, `:1645`, `:2056`) were latently broken the same way and are fixed too. Reordered the names to follow `BATCH_KEYS` rather than renumbering the key, since sorted order is main's own convention and the production consumers already follow it. Verified afterwards that all four unpacks now read `attention_mask, cu_seqlens, cu_seqlens_padded, hybrid_cp_group, labels, local_cp_size, loss_mask, max_seqlen, padding_mask, position_ids, tokens`, and that `pretrain_gpt.forward_step`'s own `BATCH_KEYS` branch already matched (its 6-/7-tuple branches use separate dev-only batch shapes and do not collide at 11). **Advisory audit:** CODEOWNERS and the dependency triple byte-identical to dev; dev-feature audit unchanged at 1356.

+# Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+
+"""Select all unit-test buckets on one CPU runner and publish the GPU matrix."""
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+import logging
+import os
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+def _actions(operation: str, *args: str) -> None:
+    # The workflow supplies the small adapter for GitHub's Node-only SDKs.
+    subprocess.run(
+        [os.environ["TESTMON_NODE"], "-e", os.environ["TESTMON_ACTIONS"], operation, *args],
+        check=True,
+    )
+
+
+def _python(script: str, args: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
+    output = subprocess.check_output(
+        [sys.executable, f"tests/unit_tests/{script}", *args], text=True
+    )
+    logger.info(output.strip())
+    return dict(line.split("=", 1) for line in output.strip().splitlines())
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    """Restore each baseline, run the existing selector, and upload its plan."""
+    if os.environ["TARGET_BRANCH"] != "main":
+        raise ValueError("Testmon selection requires main")
+    platform = os.environ["RECIPE_PLATFORM"]
+    generation = f"{os.environ['GITHUB_RUN_ID']}-{os.environ['GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT']}"
+    temporary = Path(os.environ["RUNNER_TEMP"])
+    cache_dir = Path("assets_dir/testmon")
+    plan = "assets_dir/testmon-plan/plan.json"
+    matrix = []
+    summary = [
+        "### Unit tests selection",
+        "",
+        "| Bucket | Mode | GPU required |",
+        "| --- | --- | --- |",
+    ]
+
+    # Restore sequentially: the path is part of the existing cache version.
+    for entry in json.loads(os.environ["BUCKETS"]):
+        bucket = entry["bucket"]
+        logger.info("Selecting %s", bucket)
+        identity = _python(
+            "testmon_cache.py",
+            [
+                "identity",
+                "--bucket",
+                bucket,
+                "--platform",
+                platform,
+                "--output",
+                str(temporary / "unit-testmon-identity.json"),
+            ],
+        )
+        if cache_dir.exists():
+            shutil.rmtree(cache_dir)
+        matched_key = ""
+        key_file = temporary / "unit-testmon-matched-key"
+        prefix = identity["cache_prefix"]
+        try:
+            _actions(
+                "restore", str(cache_dir), f"{prefix}lookup-{generation}", prefix, str(key_file)
+            )
+            matched_key = key_file.read_text()
+        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
+            logger.warning("Testmon cache restore failed for %s", bucket)
+        result = _python(
+            "testmon_selector.py",
+            [
+                "select",
+                "--cache-dir",
+                str(cache_dir),
+                "--bucket",
+                bucket,
+                "--platform",
+                platform,
+                "--source-sha",
+                os.environ["SOURCE_SHA"],
+                "--matched-key",
+                matched_key,
+                "--pr-files-dir",
+                os.environ["PR_FILES_DIR"],
+                "--output",
+                plan,
+            ],
+        )
+        mode, has_tests = result["mode"], result["has_tests"]
+        if (
+            mode not in {"selected", "full"}
+            or has_tests not in {"true", "false"}
+            or (mode == "full" and has_tests != "true")
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(f"Invalid Testmon selection result for {bucket}")
+        artifact = ""
+        if mode == "selected":
+            bucket_hash = hashlib.sha256(bucket.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
+            artifact = f"unit-test-plan-{platform}-{bucket_hash}-{generation}"
+            # Upload empty plans too: the coverage gate uses them as skip evidence.
+            _actions("upload", artifact, plan, "assets_dir/testmon-plan")
+        if has_tests == "true":
+            matrix.append(
+                {
+                    **entry,
+                    "mode": "preselected" if mode == "selected" else "full",
+                    "plan_artifact": artifact,
+                }
+            )
+        summary.append(f"| `{bucket}` | {mode} | {has_tests} |")
+
+    with Path(os.environ["GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"]).open("a") as stream:
+        stream.write("\n".join(summary) + "\n")
+    with Path(os.environ["GITHUB_OUTPUT"]).open("a") as stream:
+        stream.write(f"matrix={json.dumps(matrix, separators=(',', ':'))}\n")
+        stream.write(f"has_tests={str(bool(matrix)).lower()}\n")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(message)s")
+    main()

+
+"""Compatibility adapters for the deprecated Hybrid-CP batch-helper keywords."""
+
+import inspect
+import warnings
+from functools import wraps
+from typing import Callable, ParamSpec, TypeVar
+
+_Parameters = ParamSpec("_Parameters")
+_Result = TypeVar("_Result")
+_DEPRECATED_KEYWORDS = (
+    ("is_hybrid_cp", "dynamic_cp"),
+    ("hybrid_cp_group_func", "dynamic_cp_group_func"),
+)
+
+
+def deprecated_hybrid_cp_kwargs(
+    function: Callable[_Parameters, _Result],
+) -> Callable[_Parameters, _Result]:
+    """Accept old keyword names without changing positional arguments or new signatures."""
+
+    @wraps(function)
+    def wrapped(*args: _Parameters.args, **kwargs: _Parameters.kwargs) -> _Result:
+        for old_name, new_name in _DEPRECATED_KEYWORDS:
+            if old_name in kwargs:
+                if new_name in kwargs:
+                    raise TypeError(f"Cannot pass both {old_name} and {new_name}")
+                warnings.warn(
+                    f"{old_name} is deprecated; use {new_name} instead.",
+                    DeprecationWarning,
+                    stacklevel=2,
+                )
+                kwargs[new_name] = kwargs.pop(old_name)
+        return function(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    # MBridge detects THD CP support by inspecting the deprecated flag's name.
+    # Keep keyword aliases discoverable, not just accepted at call time.
+    signature = inspect.signature(function)
+    aliases = [
+        inspect.Parameter(
+            old_name,
+            inspect.Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY,
+            default=None,
+            annotation=signature.parameters[new_name].annotation,
+        )
+        for old_name, new_name in _DEPRECATED_KEYWORDS
+        if new_name in signature.parameters
+    ]
+    wrapped.__signature__ = signature.replace(parameters=[*signature.parameters.values(), *aliases])
+    return wrapped

+"""Pure topology helpers shared by dynamic CP initialization and scheduling."""
+
+from typing import List
+
+
+def get_valid_dynamic_context_parallel_group_sizes(total_size: int) -> List[int]:
+    """Return runtime CP sizes that can partition a DPxCP rank list exactly.
+
+    Power-of-two subgroups are used when they evenly divide the rank list. The
+    full DPxCP group is always valid and reuses the existing communicator.
+    """
+    if total_size < 1:
+        raise ValueError(f"Dynamic CP group size must be positive, got {total_size}")
+
+    group_sizes = []
+    group_size = 1
+    while group_size < total_size:
+        if total_size % group_size == 0:
+            group_sizes.append(group_size)
+        group_size *= 2
+    group_sizes.append(total_size)
+    return group_sizes

 # Data Pipeline
 
+Packed training and evaluation support `--pad-packed-seq-alignment N` (a CP-local
+token multiple before SP) or `max` (pad to `--max-seqlen-per-dp-cp-rank`). MXFP8
+automatically requires a multiple of 32 tokens after SP; the effective alignment
+combines that requirement with the requested multiple. Padding is added before
+CP layout construction, with masked dummy sequences and consistent THD metadata.
+The scheduler reserves an aligned capacity; padding never truncates valid tokens.
+This eager path does not require CUDA graphs.
+
+When unpacking SFT data, prompt-only sub-sequences are retained so packing can
+still fill all DP ranks; their zero loss masks exclude them from the loss. A DP
+rank can contribute no samples and still receive scheduled work. A global batch
+with no sequences is rejected on all ranks.
+
+Dynamic CP does not currently support `--deterministic-mode`, CUDA graphs, or
+router z-loss. Configuration validation rejects these combinations before training.
+Static sequence packing without dynamic CP retains its existing deterministic-mode
+support. Dynamic CP for Hybrid models follows in PR #7048.
+
+Batch helpers use `dynamic_cp` and `dynamic_cp_group_func`. The old `is_hybrid_cp`
+and `hybrid_cp_group_func` keyword arguments remain accepted with a deprecation
+warning for downstream callers. Positional arguments and the legacy
+`hybrid_cp_group` batch metadata are unchanged during this compatibility window.
+The deprecated keywords also remain visible to signature-based feature detection
+used by downstream consumers such as MBridge.
+
+The `gpt_packed_train_eval` functional test runs the real GPT entrypoint on eight
+GPUs with TP2/PP2, synthetic variable-length data, and static or dynamic packing.
+It checks finite training/evaluation losses and gradient norms, a completed
+checkpoint, and CP1/CP2 coverage in both training and evaluation. It does not
+claim deterministic or golden-loss equivalence. Run it from the repository root:
+
+```bash
+python tests/functional_tests/test_cases/gpt/gpt_packed_train_eval/run_test.py \
+  --packing-mode dynamic --output-path /path/to/a/new/output-directory
+```

+"""FlashInfer routed-MoE support for per-token NVFP4 x NVFP4 squared-ReLU and SwiGLU experts.
+
+Expert weights are quantized from MCore's BF16 expert stacks with one FP32

+per token, so no calibration or static input scale is required. The experts
+run on FlashInfer's CuTe DSL block-scaled grouped GEMMs.

+    import flashinfer
+    from flashinfer import ActivationType, SfLayout, nvfp4_quantize
+    from packaging.version import Version
+

+    if Version(flashinfer.__version__).release < (0, 7, 0):

+        )

+FLOAT4_E2M1_MAX = 6.0
+FLOAT8_E4M3_MAX = 448.0

+# global scale is the recipe constant 1 / (E4M3_MAX * E2M1_MAX). FlashInfer rejects
+# other values. It must be a Python float: a tensor triggers a host sync.

+class FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights:
+    """FC1/FC2 expert stacks in the CuTe DSL block-scaled grouped-GEMM layout.
+
+    Data is packed E2M1 ``[experts, N, K // 2]``. ``*_scale`` is the 6D MMA view
+    of the 128x4-swizzled E4M3 block scales held in ``*_scale_swizzled``.
+    ``*_alpha`` are the per-expert FP32 dequantization scales and
+    ``fc2_input_scale`` is the per-token recipe constant for the FC2 input.
+    Gated (SwiGLU) FC1 has ``2 * padded_intermediate_size`` rows in FlashInfer's
+    interleaved up/gate order.
+    """
+
+    hidden_size: int
+    intermediate_size: int
+    padded_hidden_size: int
+    padded_intermediate_size: int

+    fc1_data: torch.Tensor
+    fc1_scale_swizzled: torch.Tensor
+    fc1_scale: torch.Tensor
+    fc1_alpha: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_data: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_scale_swizzled: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_scale: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_alpha: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_input_scale: torch.Tensor
+

+    def num_local_experts(self) -> int:
+        """Number of experts in each stack."""
+        return self.fc1_data.shape[0]
+

+def _global_encode_scale(weight: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Return the one-element NVFP4 global encode scale for a weight matrix."""
+    amax = weight.abs().amax().float().reshape(1)
+    encode = (FLOAT8_E4M3_MAX * FLOAT4_E2M1_MAX) / amax
+    return torch.where(amax > 0, encode, torch.ones_like(encode))
+

+def _zero_pad(weight: torch.Tensor, padded_rows: int, padded_cols: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    rows, cols = weight.shape
+    padded = weight.new_zeros(padded_rows, padded_cols, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    padded[:rows, :cols].copy_(weight)
+    return padded
+
+
+def _pad_fc1(weight: torch.Tensor, gated: bool, padded_i: int, padded_h: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Zero-pad one FC1 expert weight into the CuTe DSL row order.
+
+    MCore stores gated FC1 as ``[gate; up]``. FlashInfer expects ``[up; gate]`` with each half
+    padded separately and the halves interleaved in ``_GLU_INTERLEAVE_ROWS``-row blocks.
+    """
+    if not gated:
+        return _zero_pad(weight, padded_i, padded_h)
+    gate, up = weight.chunk(2, dim=0)
+    halves = torch.stack((_zero_pad(up, padded_i, padded_h), _zero_pad(gate, padded_i, padded_h)))
+    blocks = halves.view(2, padded_i // _GLU_INTERLEAVE_ROWS, _GLU_INTERLEAVE_ROWS, padded_h)
+    return blocks.transpose(0, 1).reshape(2 * padded_i, padded_h)

+    padded: torch.Tensor,
+    data_out: torch.Tensor,
+    swizzled_scale_out: torch.Tensor,
+    alpha_out: torch.Tensor,

+    """Quantize one zero-padded ``[rows, cols]`` expert weight into CuTe DSL NVFP4 storage."""
+    padded_rows, padded_cols = padded.shape
+    encode = _global_encode_scale(padded)
+    data, scale = nvfp4_quantize(padded, encode, sfLayout=SfLayout.layout_128x4)
+    data_out.copy_(data.view(torch.uint8).reshape(padded_rows, padded_cols // 2))
+    swizzled_scale_out.copy_(
+        scale.view(torch.uint8).reshape(padded_rows, padded_cols // NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE)
+    )
+    alpha_out.copy_(encode.reciprocal())

+            f"FC1 shape {tuple(fc1_weight.shape)} does not match FC2 shape "
+            f"{tuple(fc2_weight.shape)}: expected [experts, intermediate or 2 * intermediate, "
+            "hidden]"
+        )
+    return experts, intermediate_size, hidden_size, gated

+def _check_refresh_metadata(
+    out, experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, padded_h, padded_i, gated
+):
+    expected = (experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, padded_h, padded_i, gated)
+    actual = (
+        out.num_local_experts,
+        out.hidden_size,
+        out.intermediate_size,
+        out.padded_hidden_size,
+        out.padded_intermediate_size,
+        out.gated,
+    )
+    if actual != expected:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "existing FlashInfer routed NVFP4 weight metadata changed across refit: "
+            f"got {actual}, expected {expected}"
+        )
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def prepare_routed_nvfp4_weights(
+    fc1_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    fc2_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    out: FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights | None = None,
+) -> FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights:
+    """Quantize BF16 squared-ReLU or SwiGLU expert stacks into the per-token NVFP4 kernel layout.
+
+    Args:
+        fc1_weight: ``[experts, intermediate, hidden]`` BF16 FC1 weights, or
+            ``[experts, 2 * intermediate, hidden]`` as MCore's ``[gate; up]`` for SwiGLU.
+        fc2_weight: ``[experts, hidden, intermediate]`` BF16 FC2 weights.
+        out: When provided, its tensors are refreshed in place. This preserves
+            addresses captured by CUDA graphs across model refits.
+    """
+    require_flashinfer_routed_nvfp4()
+    experts, intermediate_size, hidden_size, gated = _validate_stacks(fc1_weight, fc2_weight)
+    padded_h = _round_up(hidden_size, _ALIGNMENT)
+    padded_i = _round_up(intermediate_size, _ALIGNMENT)
+    fc1_rows = 2 * padded_i if gated else padded_i
+    device = fc1_weight.device
+
+    if out is None:
+
+        def _empty(*shape, dtype):
+            return torch.empty(*shape, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+
+        # Each expert's row count is a multiple of 128, so per-expert 128x4-swizzled
+        # scale blocks concatenate into the swizzled layout of the stacked matrix.
+        fc1_scale_swizzled = _empty(
+            experts * fc1_rows, padded_h // NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE, dtype=torch.uint8
+        )
+        fc2_scale_swizzled = _empty(
+            experts * padded_h, padded_i // NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE, dtype=torch.uint8
+        )
+        out = FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights(
+            hidden_size=hidden_size,
+            intermediate_size=intermediate_size,
+            padded_hidden_size=padded_h,
+            padded_intermediate_size=padded_i,
+            gated=gated,
+            fc1_data=_empty(experts, fc1_rows, padded_h // 2, dtype=torch.uint8),
+            fc1_scale_swizzled=fc1_scale_swizzled,
+            fc1_scale=convert_sf_to_mma_layout(
+                fc1_scale_swizzled, m=fc1_rows, k=padded_h, num_groups=experts
+            ),
+            fc1_alpha=_empty(experts, dtype=torch.float32),
+            fc2_data=_empty(experts, padded_h, padded_i // 2, dtype=torch.uint8),
+            fc2_scale_swizzled=fc2_scale_swizzled,
+            fc2_scale=convert_sf_to_mma_layout(
+                fc2_scale_swizzled, m=padded_h, k=padded_i, num_groups=experts
+            ),
+            fc2_alpha=_empty(experts, dtype=torch.float32),
+            fc2_input_scale=torch.full(
+                (1,), PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION_GLOBAL_SCALE, dtype=torch.float32, device=device
+            ),
+        )
+    else:
+        _check_refresh_metadata(
+            out, experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, padded_h, padded_i, gated
+        )
+
+    for expert in range(experts):
+        _quantize_expert(
+            _pad_fc1(fc1_weight[expert], gated, padded_i, padded_h),
+            out.fc1_data[expert],
+            out.fc1_scale_swizzled[expert * fc1_rows : (expert + 1) * fc1_rows],
+            out.fc1_alpha[expert : expert + 1],
+        )
+        _quantize_expert(
+            _zero_pad(fc2_weight[expert], padded_h, padded_i),
+            out.fc2_data[expert],
+            out.fc2_scale_swizzled[expert * padded_h : (expert + 1) * padded_h],
+            out.fc2_alpha[expert : expert + 1],
+        )
+    for swizzled, mma, m, k in (
+        (out.fc1_scale_swizzled, out.fc1_scale, fc1_rows, padded_h),
+        (out.fc2_scale_swizzled, out.fc2_scale, padded_h, padded_i),
+    ):
+        converted = convert_sf_to_mma_layout(swizzled, m=m, k=k, num_groups=experts)
+        if converted.data_ptr() != mma.data_ptr():
+            mma.copy_(converted)
+    return out
+
+
+def quantize_routed_nvfp4_input(
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor, padded_hidden_size: int
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Pad and quantize routed-MoE input with one FP32 scale per token.
+
+    Returns packed E2M1 data ``[tokens, padded_hidden // 2]``, linear block scales
+    ``[tokens, padded_hidden // 16]`` (as returned by FlashInfer), and FP32
+    per-token scales ``[tokens]``.
+    """
+    hidden_padding = padded_hidden_size - hidden_states.shape[-1]
+    if hidden_padding < 0:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"padded hidden size {padded_hidden_size} is smaller than input hidden size "
+            f"{hidden_states.shape[-1]}"
+        )
+    padded_hidden = F.pad(hidden_states, (0, hidden_padding)) if hidden_padding else hidden_states
+    quantized_hidden, hidden_scale, per_token_scale = nvfp4_quantize(
+        padded_hidden.contiguous(),
+        PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION_GLOBAL_SCALE,
+        sfLayout=SfLayout.layout_linear,
+        per_token_activation=True,
+    )
+    hidden_scale = hidden_scale.reshape(
+        hidden_states.shape[0], padded_hidden_size // NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE
+    )
+    return quantized_hidden, hidden_scale, per_token_scale
+
+
+def _get_cute_dsl_wrapper(
+    weights: FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights,
+    num_experts: int,
+    top_k: int,
+    local_expert_offset: int,
+    activation_type: int,
+    device: torch.device,
+):
+    # The fused finalize accumulates top-k routes with output-dtype atomics, whose
+    # order is not fixed; the two-stage finalize reduces each token's routes in order.
+    use_fused_finalize = not (
+        torch.are_deterministic_algorithms_enabled() or is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled()
+    )
+    key = (
+        use_fused_finalize,
+        num_experts,
+        top_k,
+        weights.padded_hidden_size,
+        weights.padded_intermediate_size,
+        weights.num_local_experts,
+        local_expert_offset,
+        activation_type,
+        str(device),
+    )
+    wrapper = _CUTE_DSL_WRAPPERS.get(key)
+    if wrapper is None:
+        # Persistent stream/event resources are created here, outside graph capture.
+        wrapper = CuteDslMoEWrapper(
+            num_experts=num_experts,
+            top_k=top_k,
+            hidden_size=weights.padded_hidden_size,
+            intermediate_size=weights.padded_intermediate_size,
+            use_cuda_graph=True,
+            num_local_experts=weights.num_local_experts,
+            local_expert_offset=local_expert_offset,
+            output_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            device=str(device),
+            activation_type=activation_type,
+            use_fused_finalize=use_fused_finalize,
+            quant_mode="w4a4",
+        )
+        _CUTE_DSL_WRAPPERS[key] = wrapper
+    return wrapper
+
+
+def flashinfer_routed_nvfp4_moe(
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+    routing_map: torch.Tensor,
+    probabilities: torch.Tensor,
+    weights: FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights,
+    *,
+    num_experts: int,
+    local_expert_offset: int,
+    activation_type: int,
+    out: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    token_capacity: int | None = None,
+    use_bounded_rows: bool = False,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Run the FlashInfer per-token NVFP4 squared-ReLU or SwiGLU MoE.
+
+    Rows whose routing entries are -1 contribute zero output, so a graph-stable
+    dispatcher buffer may be passed in full. When token_capacity is set and the
+    controller marks the current graph safe, only that fixed prefix is quantized
+    and processed, as for routed MXFP8; rows past it are left untouched in out.
+    """
+    require_flashinfer_routed_nvfp4()
+    expected_activation = ActivationType.Swiglu if weights.gated else ActivationType.Relu2
+    if activation_type != expected_activation.value:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{'Gated' if weights.gated else 'Non-gated'} per-token NVFP4 expert weights need "
+            f"activation_type={expected_activation.name}; got activation_type={activation_type}"
+        )
+    if hidden_states.shape[-1] != weights.hidden_size:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"hidden size {hidden_states.shape[-1]} does not match expert hidden size "
+            f"{weights.hidden_size}"
+        )
+    if probabilities.dtype != torch.float32:
+        raise TypeError(
+            f"FlashInfer routed MoE requires FP32 probabilities; got {probabilities.dtype}"
+        )
+
+    active_rows, _ = select_routed_mxfp8_active_rows(
+        hidden_states.shape[0], token_capacity=token_capacity, use_bounded_rows=use_bounded_rows
+    )
+    hidden_states = hidden_states[:active_rows]
+    routing_map = routing_map[:active_rows]
+    probabilities = probabilities[:active_rows]
+    quantized_hidden, hidden_scale, per_token_scale = quantize_routed_nvfp4_input(
+        hidden_states, weights.padded_hidden_size
+    )
+    wrapper = _get_cute_dsl_wrapper(
+        weights,
+        num_experts=num_experts,
+        top_k=routing_map.shape[1],
+        local_expert_offset=local_expert_offset,
+        activation_type=activation_type,
+        device=quantized_hidden.device,
+    )
+    output = wrapper.run(
+        quantized_hidden,
+        hidden_scale.unsqueeze(-1),
+        routing_map.to(torch.int32),
+        probabilities,
+        weights.fc1_data,
+        weights.fc1_scale,
+        weights.fc1_alpha,
+        weights.fc2_input_scale,
+        weights.fc2_data,
+        weights.fc2_scale,
+        weights.fc2_alpha,
+        per_token_scale=per_token_scale,
+    )[:, : weights.hidden_size].contiguous()
+
+    if out is not None:
+        if out.shape[0] < output.shape[0] or out.shape[1:] != output.shape[1:]:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"output buffer shape {tuple(out.shape)} cannot hold {tuple(output.shape)}"
+            )
+        out[: output.shape[0]].copy_(output)
+        return out
+    return output
